entradas.text: As I was talking to Lucian, I spotted Kesaro Kibener walking to the back of the hall towards Tarquin Soll.
Serge was driving me towards the Grand National Assembly for today's historic vote. It was a big day.
I wondered whether my attempt at changing the Constitution would end any differently than Alphonso's.
Gloria looked at Petr. She looked annoyed.
I looked out the window as the noise of the city diminished, and saw that we were already inside the Palace complex.
He abruptly turned away from me and walked towards his seat.
The Maroon Palace stood on a small hilltop surrounded by trees. We passed by the palace and entered the forest that separated it from the Grand National Assembly.
We drove on the small road that wound through the forest. It was a warm day, so I rolled down the window. I could hear birds singing from the trees.
"Let's win this, Mr. President!"
The complex housed the buildings of all government branches in the centre of Holsord. It was one of the biggest developments in Sordland.
The pace in the hall definitely increased. The groups dispersed and MPs began lining up at the ballot box.
"How many votes left?"
"Are you okay back there, sir?"
"It's looking pretty good. 20 more votes to count."
"I'm good."
"What? 50 votes left and we still need 49 more ayes. Shit!"
"Hey, Serge. I'm okay. How are you doing?"
entradas.menu: "Hey, Serge. I'm okay. How are you doing?"

entradas.text: Petr turned to me.
"I'm stressed about today."
"I'll follow you anywhere, Anton."
"I'm sure it's going to work out fine, sir."
"It's okay. There's hope."
"Don't stress yourself."
"Sir. What do we do?"
"I'm as good as I can be, sir."
"Fuck."
"That's good to hear."
"We're going to get this!"
Serge made a left turn out the forest and entered the vast garden area of the Assembly.
"I hope he doesn't sabotage the vote."
entradas.menu: "I hope he doesn't sabotage the vote."

entradas.text: "I'll go talk to him."
"Just shut up, Petr."
"Did you know that Mr. Tarquin Soll came to Holsord this morning?"
"I heard some politicians talking about it today. Apparently this is the first time he's come to the city in the last five years."
"I thought he left the mainland and lived on Duru Island, never to return to politics. But they were saying he might be here to exercise his Member of Honor rights for the first time..."
"Wait, what? Who was talking about this?"
entradas.menu: "Wait, what? Who was talking about this?"

entradas.text: "Slow down, Serge. Are you sure?"
"That's great. Maybe I'll meet him."
"That's troubling..."
"Yes sir. I overheard several men talking about it around the gardens of the Assembly."
"I'm sure you'll meet him, sir. If he's coming here after all these years, he would pay the President his respects."
"Do you think he's here because of today's vote?"
"Maybe he's here to make a statement."
entradas.menu: "Maybe he's here to make a statement."

entradas.text: "Yes, Serge. Most likely."
"He's here to show everyone he's still alive."
entradas.menu: "He's here to show everyone he's still alive."

entradas.text: "I hope not."
"The proposal will be presented to the Supreme Court shortly for the final voting procedure."
"He's probably here to make a scene."
entradas.menu: "He's probably here to make a scene."

entradas.text: "He's at the back of the hall."
entradas.menu: "He's at the back of the hall."

entradas.text: "I bet it was just some rumor. I don't think he'll appear out of nowhere."
entradas.menu: "I bet it was just some rumor. I don't think he'll appear out of nowhere."

entradas.text: He tried to get Gloria's attention by waving at her.
"Well, I'm sure he will support you, sir."
"Sorry..."
"Of course, sir. Good luck with the vote!"
"Thereby, the Grand National Assembly has decisively rejected the changes to the Constitution."
"Let's see."
"Of course he will, Serge."
"Come on..."
"I doubt that."
"What!?"
"Don't patronize me, Serge."
"We'll learn soon enough."
Suddenly, Lucian pulled me aside.
Serge drove inside the gates of the parkway and parked the car.
They cast their votes and walked away.
"Soll is here."
"I hope so too."
Petr looked uneasy.
"We have arrived, sir."
"It will."
"Thank you, Serge."
The Assembly was roaring with all kinds of different reactions.
"We'll talk later. See you, Serge."
"Thereby, the Grand National Assembly has rejected the changes to the Constitution."
"Good. I must go now."
"Good luck with the vote!"
I walked up the white stone stairs of the Grand National Assembly. The entrance looked like a temple gate from the classical era.
I walked down to join him.
The door opened to reveal vast corridors of wood and white stone. I joined the crowd of people who were walking slowly towards the parliamentary hall.
Many members of Assembly looked at me with puzzled faces. But at least the USP members seemed to hurry a little faster to the ballot box.
Suddenly, I noticed Lucian emerge from the crowd of packed politicians in front of me. He looked relieved when he saw me.
"Ah, sir. There you are. Have you seen Vice President Vectern? He's nowhere to be found."
"Yes, thank you."
"I don't think he'll miss a vote this important..."
entradas.menu: "I don't think he'll miss a vote this important..."

entradas.text: "I'm sure he's among the crowd somewhere."
entradas.menu: "I'm sure he's among the crowd somewhere."

entradas.text: "I've just arrived here, Lucian."
He pointed at the back of the Assembly, near one of the exits.
"EVERYBODY! CAST YOUR VOTE AND SIT BACK. DON'T CROWD THE HALL!"
entradas.menu: "EVERYBODY! CAST YOUR VOTE AND SIT BACK. DON'T CROWD THE HALL!"

entradas.text: "I hope you are right."
"I insist."
"As you wish, sir."
"I hope Mr. Vectern arrives soon too..."
"At any rate, how about yourself? Are you ready to finally face the Assembly, sir?"
"I can't take this. It must be valuable to you."
entradas.menu: "I can't take this. It must be valuable to you."

entradas.text: I looked at the back of the watch. It was made in 1920. I put it in my front pocket and gave my thanks to Serge. I opened the car door.
"As ready as I've ever been, Lucian."
entradas.menu: "As ready as I've ever been, Lucian."

entradas.text: "Keep it."
"Yes. I hope it works out."
He put the watch in his front pocket and I opened the car door.
"I'm still a bit stressed."
"My father would be happy."
"Lucian. I've just heard something worrying from Serge..."
entradas.menu: "Lucian. I've just heard something worrying from Serge..."

entradas.text: "Yes, sir. You are right. I will hold on to the watch myself."
"We'll address that later, sir. Come, we must go inside."
"I have full confidence in you, Mr. President."
He put the watch in his front pocket and I opened the car door.
"Very well."
"Don't be. We'll face the results now."
I took the good luck charm.
We followed the crowd into the parliamentary hall. After we were inside, Lucian and I separated to take our assigned seats. I went up to the mezzanine overlooking the hall and sat down.
"Superstitions don't help anyone, Serge."
I looked at the back of the watch. The year 1920 was engraved on it. I put it in my front pocket, gave my thanks to Serge and opened the car door.
He opened his hand and showed me a very old-looking pocket watch. It looked like it was made during the Century of Revolutions.
I waited as the MPs took their places inside the hall one by one.
"Before you go, I want you to take this. My father had this pocket watch, and he said it protected him from the evil of this world. I want you to have it."
After a while, I saw Gloria walk to her elevated seat at the center of the hall.
I felt destroyed. I lowered my head and closed my eyes for a second.
"Ladies and gentlemen..."
Petr turned to me.
"Please take your seats. We will shortly begin with today's agenda of the USP's proposed changes to the Constitution of Sordland."
After a short while, everybody was in their seats.
"Thank God!"
"According to the current Constitution, constitutional amendments require a two-thirds majority in order to reach Assembly approval."
He looked at Gloria as she and her assistants counted the votes. The Speaker's seat was only a few meters away from our platform.
"If the vote succeeds, the proposal will be sent to the Supreme Court."
We left the hall together to grab a drink at the Palace.
"The proposal in question includes these points..."
"THE CONSTITUTION IS AT STAKE! STOP WASTING YOUR TIME!"
entradas.menu: "THE CONSTITUTION IS AT STAKE! STOP WASTING YOUR TIME!"

entradas.text: "First section of the changes... Article 57 is modified with the following..."
She started reading the proposal to the Assembly.
"That's my man!"
"I mean... Maybe I was not in this exact seat, sure... But I was here in the Assembly."
It felt like an eternity had passed. Finally, she finished reading the changes.
She continued reading the proposal, highlighting each section.
"I really hope this proposal goes through..."
"...may not exercise his right to..."
Most of the MPs seemed like they were already falling asleep.
"...a simple majority is considered..."
"Goddammit!"
The seat was really hurting my back.
"I was talking to Lucian."
"...Section 4, paragraph 44a...
"136 ayes. 40 more votes to count."
"No, you were not. I was here until the voting began."
entradas.menu: "No, you were not. I was here until the voting began."

entradas.text: "...I hereby invite all of you to vote."
"You're right, but do you really think the bordello would pick up the phone this early in the day?"
"Section 2, paragraph 36..."
After I talked with Petr about the vote, we both left the hall to discuss our next steps.
She went on...
"LADIES AND GENTLEMEN! VOTE NOW FOR THE FUTURE OF SORDLAND!"
entradas.menu: "LADIES AND GENTLEMEN! VOTE NOW FOR THE FUTURE OF SORDLAND!"

entradas.text: "Not everything's about drinking, Petr."
And on...
"I was right here. Where were you?"
"...the Justices of the Supreme Court..."
"No, that's a bit too much."
Petr turned to me.
"As I previously stated, it will require a two-thirds majority in order to pass..."
She struck her gavel down. The loud bang made some MPs jump up in shock as they woke from their deep sleep.
"Yeah, let's do it."
"The usual."
"You may now cast your votes."
"Speaking of which, how about a celebratory drink?"
I felt the need to stand up and stretch. I looked down at the hall from the platform I was seated on.
"God... I'm sorry."
Some Assembly members immediately walked to the ballot box to cast their votes. Most of them, however, began to congregate in groups around the hall, discussing the changes.
"Sure."
I descended from the mezzanine down to the hall.
entradas.menu: Go down to the hall where all the MPs are.

entradas.text: "Yes. Of course."
I sat down and kept watching the Assembly.
entradas.menu: Sit back down and keep watching.

entradas.text: "Our best bet to divide the Old Guard votes is Garaci. He's the most corrupt person I've ever known."
"FOR DEMOCRACY!"
"We need 30 out of the last 40. Damn."
"I'M EXPECTING YOUR VOTES!"
"I have complete trust in you."
My voice echoed in the hall. Everybody turned and looked at me with surprise.
"Petr! How are you doing?"
"Let's enjoy this victory for now."
Gloria raised an eyebrow when she saw me.
"Orso Hawker will be a problem."
"I'M WATCHING YOU!"
"Did you cast your vote?"
"JOIN US FOR CHANGE!"
"I'll talk to the key figures of the Court. We'll be fine."
entradas.menu: "I'll talk to the key figures of the Court. We'll be fine."

entradas.text: Some USP members started to whistle and clap while others gave me puzzled looks.
"117 ayes. 50 more votes to count."
We waited for Serge by the entrance.
"Hey, where were you?"
After regathering our thoughts, Petr and I walked out of the Assembly hall.
"VOTE YES!"
"DON'T MAKE A MISTAKE!"
I followed his finger to see Tarquin Soll sitting there.
We both went back to our seats. When I returned back to the mezzanine, I saw Petr sitting in the chair next to mine.
Some of the members in the hall started to shout back at me.
"Ladies and Gentlemen of the Assembly! We will soon begin counting. Please cast your votes if you haven't already."
"Very well, we shall."
"20 votes left to count. It doesn't look good for you."
We both looked down at the floor for a while.
"SHUT UP!"
The Assembly roared with all kinds of different reactions.
"YOU WILL DO AS I SAY!"
"Now. Why don't you two get back to your seats, as well."
The shouts turned into booing, and the Assembly broke into chaos.
He looked at me with surprise.
"Mr. Soll, welcome to the Assembly!"
Gloria hit the gavel three times.
"Did you hear that? We are screwed...
<shout>"ORDER! ORDER!"</shout>
"I'm not sure."
"Gentlemen! Please! Don't you know how to cast a vote? This is not a circus!"
He walked to his seat with a fist in the air.
Some MPs started shouting back at Gloria.
"We'll fix this."
"ORDEEEEEEER!"
Petr turned to me.
She kept hitting the gavel frantically.
"Yes. If the USP abandons us, we'll form a new party."
entradas.menu: "If the USP abandons us, we'll form a new party."

entradas.text: "Ladies and gentlemen! Please have civil conversations and refrain from shouting at each other! If you are not capable of that, please leave the Assembly!"
She banged the gavel several times. The sound echoed across the room.
She looked at me.
They went ahead and cast their votes.
"Also, Mr. President. Please refrain from shouting yourself. If you want to share something with the Assembly, please ask to speak after the vote session is concluded."
"We need to hold an emergency meeting to plan our next moves."
"Thank you."
"Thereby, the Grand National Assembly has reached a two-thirds majority and accepted the changes to the Constitution."
"It's hard to be in charge without any support... well, let's see what happens."
"Don't worry. There is already a time limit and we are abiding by the rules. Assembly members are used to this process."
I saw some people cast their votes, but many were still walking around the hall or talking to each other.
"Fine, fine."
Then, I noticed Kesaro Kibener approaching.
"YES!"
He stopped below the mezzanine and looked up at me.
"You are right... So you think we can still survive this?"
I went down to the floor and approached Kesaro.
entradas.menu: Go down to talk to him.

entradas.text: I stared back down at him.
"Petr, shut up!"
We looked at each other in silence for a few moments. Finally, he spoke.
A single bang from Gloria's gavel reverberated across the hall. Everyone fell silent.
"Mr. President! How are you feeling up there? Are you comfortable?"
"Screw Soll and the party. We were always on our own."
entradas.menu: "Screw Soll and the party. We were always on our own."

entradas.text: "Not one bit."
He looked much older than he had five years ago. But I could tell he had the same fire in him. Some MP's had already gathered around him and were chattering in awe.
"What's that supposed to mean?"
"Damn it!"
"I hope you vote yes."
"Keep hoping if you want. You already know our position."
"I'm surprised to see you here, considering the way you ignored your own party. Don't worry, Mr. President. We are here. Relax."
"You were once sitting among us in the Assembly, working under the Soll administration... Don't ever forget your past."
"Soll or no Soll, we are definitely fucked. Neither the party nor the public is going to be pleased."
"You seem to be fond of your position. Try to enjoy it while you can."
"I can't do that, Mr. President."
He walked away.
"We did it!"
"I'm sorry to take so long, Mr. President. There was a *friend* who needed more clarification for his vote."
"In any case, the proposal has passed the Assembly. But now we have to think about the Supreme Court..."
Suddenly, I saw Lucian waving at me. He was among a group of people gathered in the hall.
"I doubt that, sir. I think he's here to sabotage the vote by sheer force of personality."
As soon as I reached the bottom of the stairs, Kesaro Kibener approached me.
"Mr. President! How are you feeling about the vote?"
"We can't change the Constitution, so what? We are still in charge."
entradas.menu: "We can't change the Constitution, so what? We are still in charge."

entradas.text: "Very positive."
"Not so fast. We still have the Court to pass."
entradas.menu: "Not so fast. We still have the Court to pass."

entradas.text: "I'm hoping for the best."
"What the hell was that?"
"Not so good."
"Let's get this over with, gentlemen."
"I hope you vote yes."
He turned his back and walked out the exit as two of his guards held the doors for him.
"You know I can't do that. We have already stated our decision."
The Assembly gradually went quiet as people started to notice Soll's presence in the hall.
"That's the right feeling. This whole proposal is a mistake."
"Give the title you hold the respect it deserves, Mr. President."
"The best outcome for this proposal is failure."
"That's great!"
"Even knowing you don't have our support? How optimistic of you."
"It's just the beginning."
"I have lost my respect for you, Mr. Rayne. So many problems in Sordland that must be addressed, and yet you insist on stalling us with your 'democratic' reforms..."
He smiled.
"Shit..."
"I'm surprised to see you here, considering the way you ignored your own party. Don't worry, Mr. President. We are here. Relax."
"I know you will fail. You will lose the game. And so will your entire administration."
"Watch your words now."
"You cannot do anything."
"Keep hoping, Mr. Kibener."
"I hope to be there when it happens."
He gestured at the men behind him.
"Thereby, the Grand National Assembly has surpassed a two-thirds majority and accepted the changes to the Constitution."
He turned his back and walked out the exit as two of his guards held the doors for him.
"We'll see, Mr. President."
"Congratulations, Mr. Rayne."
He laughed.
"Hell yeah, we did!"
"We have to make sure he doesn't sabotage anything."
entradas.menu: "We have to make sure he doesn't sabotage anything."

entradas.text: "I'm sorry, Mr. President. We had an issue with one vote at the last minute. I've collected them all now."
I went to the very center of the hall to shout at the crowd of people who still hadn't cast their votes.
entradas.menu: Shout at the Assembly from the center of the hall.

entradas.text: He looked at me.
Then I saw Lucian waving at me. He was among a group of people in the corner of the hall. I walked up to him.
"Good day, Mr. Clavin."
On my way, I bumped into Mansoun Leke.
"Former President Soll. Nice of you to join us."
entradas.menu: "Former President Soll. Nice of you to join us."

entradas.text: "Mr. President! I'm sorry, I didn't see you there..."
"It is time to realize that real change will only come from real reformists. The People's Freedom and Justice Party will keep leading this movement!"
"I wish you good luck with the vote."
"You of all people know the strength of his personality. We must keep the Assembly's attention focused on you and your reforms."
"Just cast your votes and let the counting begin."
entradas.menu: "Just cast your votes and let the counting begin."

entradas.text: "I respect your fight to decrease the election threshold. The Independents will be giving you our full support."
I walked to Gloria and asked her to speed up the voting.
entradas.menu: Go and ask Gloria to speed up the voting.

entradas.text: "If this succeeds, this will finally open the way for Bludish representation in the Assembly. We'll have you to thank for that."
I called out to him.
"What took you so long?"
"I respect your fight to abolish the Member of Honor position. At last, a chance to hold Tarquin Soll accountable for what he did to the Bludish people..."
"I'm also 100 percent behind your decision to abolish the Member of Honor position. At last, a chance to hold Tarquin Soll accountable for what he did to the Bludish people..."
I kept watching him as he stared at the MPs.
"The faithful and selfless servant of our nation, the distinguished face of our republic, Colonel Tarquin Soll!"
entradas.menu: "The faithful and selfless servant of our nation, the distinguished face of our republic, Colonel Tarquin Soll!"

entradas.text: "You have my support. I'd like to also see you support Bludish rights in the future. I hope you stand by us."
"Thank God he didn't do anything..."
He walked out the exit as two of his guards held the doors for him.
"The voting has been concluded."
"Today is a big day for you, after all."
He stood and gazed around the hall as all of the members of the Grand National Assembly went silent.
"It's a big day for all of us."
entradas.menu: "It's a big day for all of us."

entradas.text: Suddenly, I noticed Tarquin Soll slowly rising from his seat at the back. He seemed to be struggling, and used his cane for help.
"I hope I have your support, Mr. Leke."
entradas.menu: "I hope I have your support, Mr. Leke."

entradas.text: "Thanks for all your hard work, Petr!"
entradas.menu: "Thanks for all your hard work, Petr!"

entradas.text: "I need the independents to make it bigger."
entradas.menu: "I need the independents to make it bigger."

entradas.text: "And these must be them."
"Most of the independents will be voting yes, Mr. President."
"Good day to you, gentlemen, Madame Speaker..."
"Oh, by the way, we have 251 members today. As you can see, the Member of Honor is here. He has already cast his vote."
Albin Clavin and three other men approached us with envelopes in their hands.
"Even though we feel it doesn't address the issues we care about the most, it is still a step in the right direction."
Loud applause came from the PFJP seats.
"But I have to say... we were disappointed when we first read the proposal."
"The proposal has 179 ayes and 72 nays."
"Thank you for the nice words. You have my support too."
entradas.menu: "Thank you for the nice words. You have my support too."

entradas.text: "I hereby invite the Supreme Court to do the right thing by not ignoring the decision of a Grand National Assembly that was elected by the Sordish people!"
"I will fight for Bludish rights, Mr. Leke. Don't doubt that."
entradas.menu: "I will fight for Bludish rights, Mr. Leke. Don't doubt that."

entradas.text: "Only a few."
"Thank you. But I don't think the Bludish people are facing as many problems as in the past."
entradas.menu: "Thank you. But I don't think the Bludish people are facing as many problems as in the past."

entradas.text: The reformist MPs started applauding him.
"The problems might not be identical, but they are still there, Mr. President. Don't presume to know what the Bludish people are facing."
"Has he, now. So, Mrs. Tory, how many votes are missing?"
"I hope you stand by your words, Mr. President."
"Anyway, I've got to go cast my vote."
"His unorthodox methods of persuasion, I'm sure, have been experienced by most of us here. This is a corrupt administration we're dealing with."
Suddenly, Gloria came up behind us.
He shook my hand and walked away.
"I would advise against that right now. The Assembly must focus on the vote. Any confrontation between the two of you would draw their attention away."
"I'm sorry it disappointed you."
"Gentlemen. Why don't you go back to your seats? Let's follow the procedure."
"We have done our best, Mr. Leke."
entradas.menu: "We have done our best, Mr. Leke."

entradas.text: "He's just like his predecessors -- enjoying the privilege of the presidency while ignoring the responsibility that comes with it!"
"We didn't write it to get votes from the independents."
entradas.menu: "We didn't write it to get votes from the independents."

entradas.text: "No. You wrote it for the people of Sordland. Some of them, anyway."
"I blame the President for this result. He and his party's weak attitude towards real change doomed him from the start."
"I hope you don't ignore Bludish rights as well, Mr. President."
Seeing this, more people started to approach him.
"Leave him be."
"I've got to go cast my vote."
He bowed in front of Soll and gave him a military salute.
"The President and the USP got what they deserved! This proposal was doomed from the start."
I finally reached Lucian, by now deep in conversation with another member of our party. He excused himself and turned towards me.
"I blame the President for this result. He and his party's weak attitude towards real change doomed him from the start."
"Sir, did you vote yet? We have to be quick."
"No. Let's vote."
The MPs kept shouting in the hall. Among them, I heard Frens Ricter's voice.
I signed my vote and prepared the envelope. Together, Lucian and I walked to the center of the hall to cast our votes. He kept rushing me throughout the process.
Gloria bowed her head slightly in respect as she saw us vote. Lucian pulled on my arm and whispered in my ear.
"This is bad."
"Mr. President. We may have a problem. Tarquin Soll is here."
"The proposal has 167 ayes and 84 nays."
"What!?"
"Let's just go back to our seats. Any noise we make will distract everyone further."
entradas.menu: "Let's just go back to our seats. Any noise we make will distract everyone further."

entradas.text: "I know."
"Maybe you can address him after the vote."
"What should we do?"
The MPs kept shouting in the hall. Among them, I heard Frens Ricter's voice.
"Where is he?"
"The proposal has 166 ayes and 85 nays, failing to surpass the two-thirds majority threshold."
"When I waved at you, he was in the corridors. He must be somewhere inside the hall now."
"I also want to thank the members of the United Sordland Party for working with our party."
"You have to accelerate the voting process. We need everybody to vote as soon as possible."
"It's okay. We'll find another plan."
"I want to congratulate the members of the Assembly and the President for finally passing changes to our dusty old Constitution!"
"We should refrain from giving him the spotlight he expects."
"The proposal has 122 ayes and 129 nays. It did not even reach the number of signatures that supported it."
"We don't know what he's capable of right now. But if Assembly members see him, he might influence them against the proposal."
"If that's what you wish."
"What can he even do?"
"Indeed, sir. But how?"
"Should I talk to him?"
"Should we do something?"
"Maybe he's here to support me."
"Shut up, Petr."
"We should make people vote now!"
I leaned forward to hear the results.
"FOR SORDLAND!"
"How are you feeling about the vote?"
"Oh, nothing."
"Of course. I did promise that."
"Of course. I did promise that."
"Don't worry. We'll get through this."
"Good to hear. I'm sure we'll get through this."
"I'll go vote now. See you afterwards."
"Excuse me."
He gave me a cold stare.
"What's the rush?"
"I'll explain on the way."
Petr pointed at where Frens Ricter was sitting.
Petr pointed at where Kesaro Kibener was sitting.
"Looks like Frens over there is in our corner."
"Looks like Kesaro over there is in our corner."
Petr pointed at where Kesaro Kibener was sitting.
Petr pointed at where Frens Ricter was sitting.
"Look at Frens over there. I'm sure he was behind this mess. You shouldn't have trusted him."
"Look at Kesaro over there. I'm sure he was behind this mess. You shouldn't have trusted him."
"You're right. I knew I couldn't trust him."
entradas.menu: "You're right. I knew I couldn't trust him."

entradas.text: "It's not over yet, Petr. Don't jump to conclusions."
entradas.menu: "It's not over yet, Petr. Don't jump to conclusions."

entradas.text: "Petr. Shut. Up."
"We already knew he wasn't going to support us. I expected this."
entradas.menu: "We already knew he wasn't going to support us. I expected this."

entradas.text: "It's not over yet, Petr. Let's not get overexcited."
entradas.menu: "It's not over yet, Petr. Let's not get overexcited."

entradas.text: "Yes. He's an important ally."
"To be honest, I don't really like him."
entradas.menu: "To be honest, I don't really like him."

entradas.text: "He never really supported us, though. It's surprising."
entradas.menu: "He never really supported us, though. It's surprising."

entradas.text: "Well--"
"Well--"
"The proposal has 110 ayes and 141 nays. It did not even gather a simple majority."
"The proposal has only 70 ayes and did not even gather a simple majority."
"The proposal has 225 ayes and 26 nays. A historic result."
He straightened his tie and walked away.
"The proposal has 166 ayes and 85 nays."
I heard a chorus of angry outbursts coming from the USP seats.
"Wait. What!?"
"Order, ladies and gentlemen! Due to the Member of Honor's attendance, the two-thirds threshold corresponds to 167 votes, which the proposal has failed to reach."
I turned to Petr.
"You must be kidding me..."
"No. This can't be real."
"How can she just shift the required vote like that!?"
entradas.menu: "How can she just shift the required vote like that!?"

entradas.text: "She just did."
"...I know. This just happened."
"It looks like Gloria screwed us over..."
"I overheard several men talking about it around the gardens of the Assembly, sir. I'm not sure who they were."
"It could just be rumors, of course."
"You know better than I do, sir."
We waited for Serge by the entrance.
"...Uh, just kidding."
"Unfortunately, the proposal in question was altered after it was reviewed by the Assembly."
"Therefore, I have to go over each of the points again."
"Today is a big day."
"Let's win this together, shall we?"
"Exactly. It's a big day for all of us."
"Yes. I'm counting on the independents."
"Don't worry, we'll get this."
"I really hope so, Mr. Leke. But I wouldn't be so optimistic."
"So, you couldn't get your party together, after all."
"In any case, let's see what the results are first."
"They'll be voting yes, Mr. President."
"I really hope so."
"Now, if you'll excuse me, I've got to go cast my vote."
"You know I can't do that, Mr. President."
"Don't worry. There is already a time limit and we are abiding by the rules. Unlike you, assembly members are used to this process."
"I blame the President for this result. He and his party's obstructive attitude towards real change doomed him from the start."
"He and the USP did their best to transform our reform proposal into something unpassable."
"They listened to our concerns and added historic changes we've been campaigning for years. This is a historic achievement for the rights of the Bludish people.
"Good luck with the vote, sir."
"My family and I are all behind you. I'm sure Sordland is as well."
